card.summary: 50 GB Media Store per organization on the free tier, explicitly a HARD limit ('50 GB Media Store per organization (hard limit)'), plus 10 GB database storage...

free_tier.stated: 50 GB Media Store per organization on the free tier, explicitly a HARD limit ('50 GB Media Store per organization (hard limit)'), plus 10 GB database storage per database. Pro raises Media Store to 250 GB then $0.05/GB-mo, database storage 10 GB then $0.80/GB-mo.

egress.terms: Not separately metered; storage is the billed dimension. Serving via Deploy endpoints is capped by compute (up to 1 vCPU / 2 GB on free).

record.tooling: Python-native: `pxt.create_dir`, `pxt.create_table`, insert of images/video/audio/documents; the SDK is the client. Open-source core, so self-hosting is possible. No S3/WebDAV surface on the cloud tier.
record.chaining: Per ORGANIZATION, so org multiplication is the only route, and the docs frame 50 GB as a hard cap designed to stop exactly that. 10 TiB would need 205 orgs.
record.limits_note: 50 GB hard per org, 10 GB per database, 1 vCPU / 2 GB per database/service on free. The word 'hard limit' means there is no overage path at all. Uploads fail rather than bill.
record.reliability_note: Small vendor; the product is really a declarative multimodal database rather than a blob store, so using it as bulk storage fights its data model (it wants typed columns, not opaque blobs).

evidence.proved: read live: '50 GB Media Store per organization (hard limit)'; '10 GB database storage per database'; Pro '250 GB Media Store per organization, then $0.05 / GB-mo'
